en: O Agni, you are born from the heavens; you, O seeker of flame, are born from the waters, from the stone, from the forests, and from the plants; O Lord of men, you are born pure.
O Agni, yours is the office of the Hotṛ, yours the seasonal office of the Potṛ; yours is the office of the Neṣṭṛ, and you are the Āgnīdhra for the one who follows the Truth.
Yours is the office of the Praśāstṛ; you act as the Adhvaryu; you are both the Brahman and the Lord of the House within our home.
O Agni, you are Indra, the bull among the virtuous; you are Viṣṇu, the wide-striding, worthy of homage.
You are the Brahman, the winner of wealth, O Brahmaṇaspati; you, O Ordainer, are accompanied by Purandhi.

O Agni, you are King Varuṇa, whose laws are firm; you become Mitra, O wonder-worker, worthy of praise. You are Aryaman, the lord of the virtuous, whose enjoyment is shared; you are Aṃśa, O God, who distributes portions at the assembly.
O Agni, as Tvaṣṭṛ, you bestow great heroism upon the worshipper; O you of Mitra-like greatness, the divine wives are your kin.
You, the swift impeller, grant us excellent horses; you are the host of men, rich in many treasures.
O Agni, you are Rudra, the Asura of the great heaven; you are the host of Maruts, and you rule over nourishment.
You travel with the ruddy winds of the mountains; as Pūṣan, you yourself protect those who worship you.
O Agni, you are the giver of wealth to the one who serves you; you, O God, are Savitṛ, the bestower of jewels.
You, O Lord of men, are Bhaga and rule over all riches; you are the protector in the home for him who has devoted himself to you.

O Agni, the clans seek you out in the home as their lord; they strive toward you, the king who is easy to find. O you of beautiful countenance, you rule over all things; you are equal to ten hundred thousand.
O Agni, men seek you as a father with their sacrifices; they seek you, the radiant one, for brotherhood through their ritual labor.
You become a son to him who honors you; as a most gracious friend, you protect us from assault.
O Agni, you are Rbhu, to be honored nearby; you are the lord of strength and of wealth consisting of cattle.
You shine forth according to your skill for the sake of giving; you are the one who instructs and extends the sacrifice.

O Agni, you are Aditi to the donor, O God; you, as Hotrā Bhāratī, grow strong through our song. You are Iḷā for a hundred winters, for the sake of skill; you are Sarasvatī, the slayer of Vṛtra, O Lord of Wealth.
O Agni, well-sustained, you are the highest vital power; in your desirable color, in your appearance, are the splendors.
You are the great, far-reaching strength; you are abundant wealth, wide on every side.
O Agni, the Ādityas have made you their mouth; the pure ones have made you their tongue, O Sage. Those who bestow gifts attend to you at the sacrifices; in you the gods eat the offered oblation.
In thee, O Agni, all the immortal, guileless gods eat the offered oblation with their mouths;
through thee mortals make their drink savory. Thou hast been born as the pure embryo of the plants.

O Agni, well-born god, you are equal to them and even surpasses them in your might; you excel them, O god, when your power spreads here through its greatness over both heaven and earth, the two world-halves.

O Agni, those wise patrons who bestow upon the singers a gift preeminent in cattle and adorned with horses—lead both us and them toward greater prosperity; may we, blessed with heroic sons, speak aloud at the assembly.

Increase Jātavedas by means of sacrifice; worship Agni with oblation and with continuous song—the one who is kindled, the one who provides excellent nourishment, the one who leads men to heaven, the celestial Hotṛ-priest seated at the pole within the sacrificial assemblies.

The nights and the dawns have lowed toward you, O Agni, as milch-cows toward their calf in the stalls. Like the chariot-pole of heaven, you shine through the human generations, O possessor of many boons, illuminating the nights in succession.

The gods have established him at the foundation of the region, the one of wondrous deeds, the messenger between heaven and earth— Agni, who is like a chariot to be recognized, with brilliant luster, and like Mitra, worthy of praise among the people.
Him, growing in his own home within the mid-air, they have placed like a shining moon in the cloud;
the winged one of Pṛśni, who observes with his eyes, following both races like a guardian of the path.
He, the Hotṛ-priest, encompassing the entire sacrifice, him men honor with oblations and song;
golden-bearded and flickering among the growing plants, he makes himself manifest throughout heaven and earth like the sky with its stars.
Enkindled for our well-being, O wealthy one, shine upon us with your light, bestowing wealth upon us.
O Agni, bring heaven and earth to us for our prosperity, so that the gods may enjoy the oblations of man.
O Agni, grant us great gifts; grant us thousandfold wealth. Open up for us the doors of booty as if with fame.
Make heaven and earth inclined toward us by means of our prayer. Like the bright sky, make the dawns shine forth.

Kindled after the dawns and nights, Agni shines like the sun with his ruddy luster; through the invocations of man, he is the one who performs the sacrifice well—the king of the people and the gracious guest for the living man.
Thus, O Agni, primeval one, has human prayer been made to swell among the immortals in the high heavens;
like a cow yielding milk for the singer within the enclosures, it has by itself impelled food of a hundredfold forms.
O Agni, may we, through our horse or through our sacred prayer (*brahman*), distinguish ourselves above these people.
May our splendor shine forth high over the five tribes, like the invincible sun.
Be mindful of us, O powerful one, as the one worthy of praise, in whom the well-born patrons find their strength;
O Agni, you who shine brightly in your own home for the sake of constant offspring, to that sacrifice the prize-winners approach.
O Jātavedas Agni, may we both—your singers and your wise patrons—abide in your protection.
Grant us wealth that is most splendid, abundant, rich in progeny, and blessed with noble offspring.

O Agni, those wise patrons who bestow upon the singers a gift preeminent in cattle and adorned with horses—lead both us and them toward greater prosperity; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Kindled on the earth, Agni has been established; he stands facing all living beings.
The purifying Hotṛ, wise from of old, may the god Agni, being worthy, worship the gods.
Narāśaṃsa, anointing the stations, equal to the three heavens in greatness, possessing self-radiance—
sprinkling the oblation with a mind that drips ghee, may he anoint the gods at the head of the sacrifice.
O Agni, being impelled by our mind as is your due, sacrifice to the gods today before the human [priest].
Bring hither the unshakable host of the Maruts; O men, worship Indra as he sits upon the sacrificial grass.
O divine sacrificial grass, increasing, rich in heroes, spread upon this altar for the sake of wealth and easy to bear—
sit upon it, O Vasus, anointed with clarified butter, all you gods, Ādityas, worthy of sacrifice!
May the divine doors, wide and easy of access, be thrown open as they are invoked with salutations.
May they, spacious and undecaying, spread themselves out, purifying their glorious and heroic luster.
Excellent are the deeds of you two who have grown great from of old, Dawn and Night, like two joyful female weavers;
weaving together the outspread thread, you two who face each other, well-milking and full of milk, are the ornament of the sacrifice.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, most wise, shall perform the sacrifice straightly with the verse, they who are most beautiful;
sacrificing to the gods at the proper times, they anoint [the offerings] upon the navel of the earth, on the three ridges.
May Sarasvatī, who perfects our devotion, the goddess Iḷā, and the all-conquering Bhāratī—
may these three goddesses, sitting upon this sacred grass (barhis) by their own inherent power, protect us with an unbroken refuge.
Tawny-hued, well-supported, bestowing vital strength, a hero is born through obedience, one who loves the gods.
May Tvaṣṭṛ open up our lineage; then may he go to the path of the gods.

May the Lord of the Forest stand by, releasing [the victim]; may Agni, through our prayers, prepare the oblation. May the divine slaughterer, knowing well, lead the thrice-anointed offering to the gods.
Ghee has been mixed; ghee is his womb; he rests in ghee; ghee is his abode.
According to your wont, bring [the gods] here; rejoice; O Bull, carry the oblation consecrated with Svāhā!
I invoke for you Agni, the brightly shining, the one worthy of perfect praise, the guest of the people, the one well-provided with offerings—
he who, like Mitra, is to be cherished, the god among the godly folk, Jātavedas.
Worshipping him in the gathering place of the waters, the Bhr̥gus twice established him among the clans of man.
May this Agni, the messenger of the gods, whose horses are swift, surpass all the worlds.

The gods have established Agni among the human clans as their beloved, like those seeking to dwell with a friend. May he shine upon the longing nights—he who is worthy of honor in the house of the donor.
His growth is delightful like that of his own body; for beautiful is the sight of him when he speeds forth, eager to act.
He who repeatedly extends his tongue among the plants shakes off his tail like a chariot-horse.
When the forest-dwellers praised my monstrous form, he fashioned a color for the Uśij; he shone with brilliant, lovely luster—he who, though aged, has suddenly become young again.
He who shines upon the forests like one parched with thirst, he has roared like water on a path, or like a chariot;
he whose path is black, the glowing and delightful one, has become manifest, smiling like the sky with its clouds.
He who has spread himself abroad over the wide earth, like a beast that wanders unherded and self-willed,
Agni, the radiant one, burning through the brushwood with his blackened path, has made the earth seem as if it were tasteless.
Now, in the remembrance of your former favor, this prayer has been recited at the third assembly.
O Agni, grant us great wealth consisting of many heroes, abundant food, and riches accompanied by noble offspring.
O Agni, just as through you the Gṛtsamadas, winning in secret, may overcome their neighbors,
so grant that vital strength to our patrons and to the singer— one that brings excellent heroes and overcomes the malicious.
The conscious Hotṛ has been born as a father for the protection of the fathers;
may we be able to harness him, the noble wealth manifest before us, who is the winner of prizes.
In whom the seven rays are extended, the leader of the sacrifice—
he, like Manu, as the Potṛ priest, impels that entire divine eighth [ray].
Or when he has run forth after them and has uttered the sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*), he then wins them;
he encompasses all poetic insights (*kāvyā*) as the felly encompasses the wheel.
For together with the pure one, the pure Praśāstṛ has been born through his mental power;
knowing his firm laws, he grows like branches.
These milch-cows, seeking their own color, have followed him, the Neṣṭṛ-priest;
are they not better than the three sisters who have gone to this place?
When the sister has approached the mother bringing clarified butter,
the Adhvaryu rejoices at their arrival like grain at the coming of rain.
May he himself prepare the officiant for his own nourishment;
may we truly win the hymn and the sacrifice, for we have offered them.
So that the wise one may prepare it properly for all the worshipful gods—
this sacrifice, O Agni, which we have performed, rests within you.
O Agni, accept this my fuel-stick and this my attendance; truly, hear these songs of praise.
With this, O Agni, son of strength, seeker of horses, we shall worship thee with this hymn,
O well-born one.
As such, O lover of songs, we who desire wealth and seek to serve thee, shall honor thee with our hymns, O giver of riches.
May he be our wise patron, O Maghavan, Lord of Wealth, Giver of Riches;
drive away from us all enmities.
May he bring us rain from heaven; may he bring us unassailable strength;
may he bring us thousandfold nourishments.
O youngest messenger, being praised with our song for the sake of the one who seeks help, come hither, O most excellent sacrificer and invoker!
For you, O Agni, O sage, go between both races as one who knows them;
like a messenger belonging to the people, you are a friend to men.
As one who knows, satisfy us; as one who is wise, worship in due order, and sit down upon this sacred grass.
O Agni, youngest descendant of Bharata, bring us the most excellent, radiant,
and much-desired wealth, O Vasu.
May the hostility of neither god nor mortal prevail over us; deliver us from that and from our enemies.
And with you, may we cross over all enemies, as one crosses over streams of water.
O Agni, pure, purifying, and worthy of praise, you shine forth mightily when offered oblations of clarified butter.
O Agni, descendant of Bharata, you are ours, being invoked with offerings of heifers, bulls, and eight-footed mares.
The wood-eater, whose libation is clarified butter, the ancient, excellent Hotṛ-priest,
the wonderful son of strength.
Like one seeking prize-winning chariots, now praise the yoking of Agni,
the most glorious and bountiful.
He who is a good leader for the donor, who, being undecaying, causes the enemy to decay; he whose countenance is beautiful when invoked with oblations.
He who is praised for his glory in his homes at evening and at dawn—
he whose sacred law (*vrata*) is never violated.
He who, like the sun with its radiance, shines forth with his flame, resplendent, anointed with ageless [powers].
Following Atri, they have magnified Agni with hymns according to his own sovereignty;
he has assumed all glories.
Through the aid of Agni, Indra, Soma, and the gods, may we remain unharmed and overcome those who attack us.
The Hotṛ priest, knowing his place, has sat down upon the seat of the Hotṛ—resplendent, shining, and most skillful.
Agni, whose wisdom protects his unfailing vows, the most excellent one with a pure tongue, brings a thousandfold wealth.
You are our messenger, and you are our protector from afar; O Bull, you are the leader to better fortune.
O Agni, for the extension of our progeny and our bodies, be a watchful guardian, shining brightly and never negligent.
Let us worship thee in thy highest birth, O Agni; let us worship with hymns in thy lower dwelling-place.
That womb from which thou hast arisen, I sacrifice to it; into thee, when well-kindled, they have poured the oblations.
O Agni, most skilled in sacrifice, worship with the oblation; quickly acknowledge the gift and the bounty.
For you are the lord of riches among all treasures; you are the inspirer of the pure word.
Both your treasures, O wonder-worker, do not diminish day by day as you are born.
Make your singer, O Agni, possessed of food; make him the lord of wealth consisting of noble offspring.

With your excellent host, O most gracious one, may you, the best of sacrificers, bring the gods to us for our well-being. As an undeceived guardian and our protector from afar, O Agni, shine forth with splendor and wealth.
Agni is the first to be invoked like a father when he has been kindled by man at the place of the sacrificial food;
clothed in splendor, immortal, and wise, he is the one to be polished, the seeker of renown, the prize-winner.
May Agni of the brilliant luster, the immortal and wise one, hear my invocation with all my songs.
Two dark steeds, or two ruddy ones, or two red ones draw his chariot; he, the far-reaching one, has fashioned it.
Upon her who lies supine, they brought forth the well-born one; Agni became the embryo within those of many forms.
Even in the dark night, the wise one dwells unconfined by his own splendors.
I sprinkle Agni with the oblation of clarified butter— he who dwells facing all beings,
broad and vast with transverse vigor, most expansive, impetuous, and visible through his foods.
I offer [oblations] from all sides to him who faces us; may he accept that with a mind free from malice.
Agni, possessing the beauty of a youth and a desirable hue, flickering with his body, cannot be touched.
O Victorious One, may you be known as the one who receives his portion by choice; with you as our messenger, let us speak like Manu.
With my tongue and eloquence, I repeatedly invoke the perfect Agni, the gatherer of wealth, who is rich in honeyed offerings.
Hear our call, O Indra; do not neglect us. May we be yours for the giving of riches, for these offerings increase your strength, seeking wealth as rivers flow.
Release the great waters, O Indra, which you caused to swell—the many that were obstructed by the serpent, O Hero.
Strengthened by hymns, you shattered even the Dāsa who considered himself immortal.
O Hero Indra, in these hymns of praise wherein you take delight, and in these lauds of the Rudras—
these [streams] flow forth for you alone, in which you rejoice, like brilliant steeds rushing toward Vāyu.
Increasing your brilliant strength and placing the brilliant thunderbolt in your arms,
O Indra, may you, growing strong and resplendent among us, overcome the Dāsa clans with the help of Sūrya.
The hidden, secret, and concealed one, dwelling within the waters and veiled therein—
the wily serpent who had propped up the waters and the sky— you slew him, O Hero, by your valor.
O Indra, let us now praise your ancient greatness, and let us also praise your recent deeds.
Let us praise the thunderbolt yearning in your arms; let us praise your two bay steeds, the banners of the sun.

O Indra, your two bay steeds, seeking booty, have now let out their neighing that drips with clarity. The earth has spread itself out in every direction; even the mountain, though about to flee, has come to rest.
The mountain sat down, never failing; bellowing, he has cried out together with his mothers.
Strengthening their voice on the far shore, they have spread abroad the breath impelled by Indra.
Indra struck down Vṛtra, the wielder of magic powers, who lay across the great river;
at the roar of this bull and his thunderbolt, the two worlds, Rodasī, trembled in fear.
The thunderbolt of this bull roared aloud when he, the human, consumed the non-human;
having drunk the pressed juice, he struck down the magical powers of the guileful Dānava.
Drink, drink the Soma, O heroic Indra! Let the exhilarating pressed juices delight you.
Filling your two flanks, let them increase your strength; thus the pressed juice has helped Indra in his many deeds.
In thee, O Indra, we have become inspired poets; may we win wisdom, serving according to the Eternal Law.
Seeking thy help, we meditate upon thy praise; may we instantly be ready for the granting of thy riches.
May we be yours, O Indra, those who, seeking your aid, increase your strength.
Grant us that most powerful wealth, rich in heroes, which you, O God, have delighted in.
Bestow upon us a dwelling, bestow a friend; O Indra, bestow upon us the host of Maruts—those who, being of one accord and rejoicing, drink the first draught along with the Vāyus.

May they come now, in whom you take delight; drink the Soma to your satisfaction, O Indra, with firm resolve! As a deliverer in battles, you have truly strengthened us, making the sky lofty with your great hymns of praise.
Those great ones who, O Deliverer, have indeed sought to win your favor with hymns,
spreading the sacred grass for the dwelling— favored by you alone, O Indra, they have gone forth to the prize.

O Hero, rejoicing indeed among the fierce ones, drink the Soma at the Trikadruka rites; O Indra, shaking your beard while being gratified, come with your two bay steeds to the drinking of the pressed juice.
Take up that power, O Hero, by which you struck down Vṛtra, the Dānu, and Aurṇavābha. You disclosed the light for the Ārya; the Dasyu was cast down on your left, O Indra.
May we, overcoming all rivals with your aids, conquer the Dasyus through the Ārya;
for us, you delivered Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, to Trita as a gift for your friendship.
As he grew strong, he struck down Arbuda with this exhilarating pressed juice of Trita;
Indra, accompanied by the Aṅgirases, rolled it away like the wheel of the sun and rent Vala asunder.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
grant it to those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
He who, as soon as born, was the first wise god and surpassed the gods by his power;
at whose breath the two worlds trembled through the greatness of his manly might—he, O people, is Indra.
He who steadied the trembling earth, who set the agitated mountains at rest,
who measured out the wide mid-air, and who propped up the sky— he, O people, is Indra.

He who, having slain the dragon, released the seven rivers; he who drove out the cows by breaking open the enclosure of Vala; he who generated fire between the two stones—he, O people, is Indra, the destroyer in battles.
He by whom all these things were made to tremble, who cast the Dāsa race down into the depths;
he who, like a winning gambler, seized the stake—the prosperity of the enemy—he, O people, is Indra.

When they ask of that terrible one, "Where is he?", and people say of him, "He does not exist," he destroys the prosperity of the enemy like a gambler's stakes; place your faith in him, O people—he is Indra.

He who is the inciter of the weary, he who is the helper of the emaciated, he who is the protector of the suppliant Brahmin and the singer; he who is the guardian of the one who has set the pressing-stones in motion and has pressed the Soma—he, O people, is Indra.
He in whose direction are horses, in whose are cattle, in whose are villages, and in whose are all chariots;
he who begot the sun and the dawn, he who is the leader of the waters—he, O people, is Indra.
He whom the two contending armies invoke, the enemies both near and far;
whom two men, mounted upon the very same chariot, call upon separately—he, O people, is Indra.
Without whom people do not conquer, whom those engaged in battle invoke for protection;
he who has become the counterpart of the universe, he who shakes the unshakable—he, O people, is Indra.
He who with his arrow struck down those who repeatedly committed great sin against me while they were unaware;
he who does not yield to the arrogance of the defiant one; he who is the slayer of the Dasyu—he, O people, is Indra.
He who discovered Śambara dwelling in the mountains in the fortieth autumn;
he who slew the dragon Ahi as he displayed his power, the Dānu lying there—he, O people, is Indra.
He who, the bull with seven rays, the mighty one, released the seven rivers to flow;
he who, thunderbolt-armed, struck down Rauhiṇa as he was scaling heaven—he, O people, is Indra.
Even Heaven and Earth bow down before him; even the mountains tremble at his might.
He who is the drinker of Soma, whose arms are braced and whose hand holds the thunderbolt—he, O people, is Indra.
He who aids with his protection the one who presses the juice, the one who cooks, the one who recites, and the one who exerts himself;
he for whom prayer is the strengthener, for whom Soma is the strengthener, and for whom this gift is the strengthener—he, O people, is Indra.
O you who, even against the stubborn, shatter strength for the one who presses the juice and cooks the oblation—you are indeed truly real.
O Indra, may we, your friends forever, with heroic sons, proclaim our wisdom at the assembly.
The Season is his mother; as soon as he was born, he entered her waters, in which he grows. Then she became a swelling cow, rich in milk; that first cream of the stalk is worthy of praise.

They come together, carrying milk; they bring nourishment for him who possesses all abundance. The path is common for those rushing down the slopes; that which you performed first—this is worthy of praise.
One follows after him as he gives; another goes along, fashioning those forms from those waters.
One endures all the repulsions of the other—he who performed this first deed: he is worthy of praise.
Distributing nourishment to all creatures, they sit like wealth upon a back that prevails for the one who approaches.
With insatiable jaws he eats the father’s food; you who performed this first deed—you are worthy of praise.
You made the earth visible to heaven, O slayer of the serpent, when you cleared the paths of the rivers;
as such, the gods have generated you, a god, with hymns like strong steeds with water—you are worthy of praise.
You who bestow both food and increase, have milked the dry from the moist, the honeyed;
you have laid down a treasure for Vivasvat. You alone rule over all; worthy of praise are you.
You who, by your law, have established in the gift-bestowing [earth] both the flowering plants and the fruit-bearing trees,
and who have generated from heaven the peerless lightnings— you, O wide one, encompassing the expanses on every side, are worthy of praise.
You who brought Nārmara together with his wealth to be slain, for the sake of nourishment and for Dāsaveśa;
you who opened the unguarded mouth of Ūrjayantī—even so today, O doer of many deeds, you are worthy of praise.

Whether it was a hundred or ten whom you helped at once when you were pleased with one, and when you protected the one who urged you on—you subdued the Dasyus for Dabhīti without using a rope; you became a true protector, O worthy of praise.
All the enclosures yielded to his manly power; they bestowed wealth upon him, the doer of great deeds.
You have propped up the six regions and the five directions; you have surpassed all others—you are worthy of praise.
O hero, your heroic power is well-proclaimed, in that by a single resolve you win wealth;
O Indra, you who have performed all the deeds of Jātūṣṭhira, the victorious one—of him you are worthy of praise.
You brought to rest the swift-flowing streams for easy crossing; you made a path for Turvīti and Vayya.
You raised up Parāvṛj when he was lowly, and you brought glory to the blind and the lame; worthy of praise, you are to be extolled.
O Vasu, prepare for us that bounty to be given; great is your wealth. O Indra, bestow that wondrous gift which brings fame day after day. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Adhvaryus, bring the Soma for Indra;
pour out the exhilarating juice with the ladles, for the hero is ever desirous of its drink. Offer it to the bull; indeed, this is what he desires.
O Adhvaryus, bring this [Soma] to him who struck down Vṛtra—who had obstructed the waters—just as a thunderbolt strikes a tree;
for he is subject to that power. This Indra is worthy of drinking it.
O Adhvaryus, him who struck down Dṛbhīka, who drove out the cows, and who opened Vala for you—
wrap this Indra with Soma-offerings like the wind in the mid-air, as one wraps a swift steed with cloths.
O Adhvaryus, urge that Indra toward the offering of Soma— he who slew Uraṇa as he looked upon his ninety-nine arms, and who cast Arbuda down and crushed him.

O Adhvaryus, to that Indra for whom you have slain Aśna, Śuṣṇa the insatiable, and Vyaṃsa; to him for whom you have slain Pipru, Namuci, and Rudhikrā—to that Indra, offer the oblation of the soma-juice.
O Adhvaryus, bring the Soma for this Indra, who shattered the hundred ancient fortresses of Śambara like stones,
and who scattered the hundred thousand followers of Varcin.
O Adhvaryus, bring the Soma for him who, having slain [the foe], buried a hundred and a thousand in the lap of the earth;
he subdued the heroes of Kutsa, Ayu, and Atithigva. Bring the Soma for him!
O Adhvaryus, whatever you men desire, bring that to Indra through your obedience;
O performers of sacrifice, bring the Soma purified by the hands to the famous Indra and offer it to him.

O Adhvaryus, perform obedience for him; pour forth the Soma purified in the wooden vat into the wooden vessel. Receiving it with joy, he has bellowed toward the offering in your hand; offer the intoxicating Soma to Indra.
O Adhvaryus, fill the liberal Indra with Soma-draughts, as one fills a cow with milk;
I know this secret of his, for the worshipful one perceives me as desiring to give more.

O Adhvaryus, him who is the king of celestial wealth, of earthly wealth, and of that which dwells upon the earth—fill him with Soma-offerings as one fills a granary with barley; let Indra be yours for this work.
O Vasu, prepare for us that gift of wealth to be given; great is your treasure.
O Indra, bestow wondrous riches day after day for the sake of glory. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly of the wise.
Now, indeed, I shall proclaim the great, true deeds of this great and true one.
At the Trikadruka festivals, he drank of this pressed soma; in its exhilaration, Indra slew the dragon.
He propped up the vast sky where there was no pillar; he filled the two worlds and the mid-air.
He supported the earth and spread it out—these things Indra did in the intoxication of Soma.
Like dwellings, he measured out the eastward-flowing channels with his measures; with his thunderbolt, he pierced the beds of the rivers.
He released them to flow freely along paths for long journeys—those deeds Indra performed in the intoxication of Soma.
Having surrounded his assailants out of fear of deception, he cast all their weapons into the kindled fire;
in the intoxication of Soma, Indra performed these deeds—he united them with cattle, horses, and chariots.

He brought to rest that great roaring river as it flowed; he carried those who did not swim across in safety. Having emerged from the water, they set out toward wealth. Indra performed these deeds in the intoxication of Soma.
By his greatness he caused the ocean to flow downward; with his thunderbolt he crushed the Dawns.
Severing those who were powerless with the swift [thunderbolts], Indra performed these deeds in the intoxication of Soma.
Knowing the secret hiding place of the maidens, he, the rejected one, rose up becoming manifest. Śroṇa stood up; Vyanaṅga looked out. Indra performed those deeds in the intoxication of Soma.

Praised by the Aṅgirases, Indra split Vala; he tore apart the firm foundations of the mountain. He caused their artificial enclosures to flow open; those deeds Indra performed in the intoxication of Soma.
Having overcome Cumuri and Dhuni with sleep, you struck down the Dasyu; you protected Dabhīti.
Even the pillar found gold there; those deeds Indra performed in the intoxication of Soma.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
grant it to those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
To you, the most excellent among the virtuous, I bring a fine hymn of praise, like an oblation into a kindled fire.
We invoke for our protection Indra—the ageless one who makes others age, the grown one who from of old is ever young.
Without whom, the great Indra, nothing exists; in him all heroic powers are concentrated.
In his belly he bears the Soma, in his body great strength, in his hand the thunderbolt, and in his head wisdom.
Neither the two worlds nor the oceans can encompass your power, O Indra; neither the mountains nor the seas can contain your chariot.
No one can reach your thunderbolt when you fly across many leagues with your swift steeds.
For all bring their will to him, the worshipful, the bold, the bull who attends to them.
As a bull, sacrifice with the oblation, you who are most wise; O Indra, drink the Soma with your bull-like luster.
The vessel of the bull flows forth, a wave of honey, for the bull to drink—the bull who is the source of food.
The two bull-like Adhvaryu priests and the bull-like pressing-stones press the bull Soma for the bull [Indra].
Mighty is your thunderbolt, and mighty is your chariot; mighty are your two bay steeds, and your weapons are like bulls.
O Bull Indra, you are the lord of the mighty exhilarating draught; satisfy yourself with the bull, the Soma.
Like a ship on the sea, I approach you with my prayer at the libations, bold in my resolve.
Will he not surely take heed of this our speech? We pour ourselves out to Indra like a fountain of wealth.
Turn toward us before the distress comes, as a cow, swelling with the pasture, turns to her calf;
O Lord of a Hundred Powers, may we once more be united with your favors, as bulls are joined with their mates.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
grant gifts to those who praise you, let not our fortune fail us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Sing this new song for him in the manner of the Aṅgirases, when his ancient powers surge forth;
when, in the exhilaration of Soma, he by his might has shattered all the enclosures of the cattle-pens that were firmly established.
May he be such a one who, measuring out his vigor for the first nourishment, surpassed all greatness;
the hero who, girding his body for battles, fastened the sky upon his head by his majesty.
You performed your first great heroic deed when, at the beginning, you stirred up your fury by means of sacred power (*brahman*).
O Lord of the bay horses, by means of him who stands upon the chariot, the swift ones, being set in motion, flow forth together yet separately.
Then he, who by his might surpassed all worlds, grew strong as a sovereign lord;
then the bearer of light overspread the two worlds with radiance, weaving together and enveloping the turbid darkness.

He, by his might, made firm the mountains facing the east; he turned the waters of the rivers downward. He supported the earth that nourishes all, and by his creative power (māyā) he propped up the sky from falling.
That [bolt] was fashioned for his two arms by his father, taken from all that exists, from the very source of being;
with it, the loudly roaring one struck down Krivi upon the earth so that he might lie there, having pierced him with the thunderbolt.

Like an aged woman dwelling with her parents, I have come from our common seat to seek you, O Bhaga. Grant me a sign; bestow it upon me and bring it hither. Give me a portion for my body, with which you may honor me.
O Indra, we would call upon you, the liberal giver; for you, O Indra, bestow works and spoils of war.
Help us, O Indra, with your wondrous aid; O bull-like Indra, make us more prosperous.
Surely may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours, O Indra, yield its boon to the singer;
grant it to those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.

At dawn, the new chariot has been yoked—the prize-winning one, with four poles, three shafts, and seven reins; ten-wheeled, man-like, and winning the light of heaven, it has become swift through our offerings and prayers.
He is prepared for him at the first, at the second, and also at the third—He, the Hotṛ-priest of Manu. Others have brought forth the germ of another; He, the noble bull, unites with others.
I shall now yoke the two bay steeds to Indra’s chariot with a new and well-spoken word, so that he may come.
Let not the many other wise sacrificers detain you here.
Come, O Indra, with two bay horses; come with four, come with six, being summoned;
come with eight, with ten, to the drinking of the Soma. This [juice] has been pressed; O bounteous one, do not neglect it!
Come hither with twenty, with thirty, or with forty bay horses, yoking them; come, O Indra, with fifty well-yoked chariots, or with sixty, or with seventy, for the drinking of the Soma.
Come hither with eighty, with ninety, or being borne by a hundred bay horses;
for this Soma among the Śunahotras has been poured out for you, O Indra, out of devotion to you, for your exhilaration.
Come toward my prayer, O Indra; yoke both bay steeds to the pole of your chariot.
For you have become one to be invoked in many places; O hero, rejoice at this libation.
May my friendship with Indra never fail; may his sacrificial gift yield for us.
Under his highest protection, within his outstretched arms, may we be victors in every endeavor.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
grant it to those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The wise have drunk of this pressed juice for exhilaration, of the nourishing food;
in which Indra, increasing from of old, has established his dwelling, as have the men devoted to sacred prayer.
Intoxicated by this mead, Indra, thunderbolt in hand, rent asunder the dragon that obstructed the floods;
when, like birds toward their nests, the refreshments from the rivers streamed forth.
That mighty Indra, slayer of Ahi, drove the flood of waters toward the ocean;
he generated the sun, found the cattle, and established the ordinances of days by means of the night.
Indra has bestowed many invincible gifts upon the man who offers oblations; he slays Vṛtra, he who has become instantly accessible to men contending for the acquisition of the sun.
Indra, the god, being praised, released the sun for the mortal who presses the soma;
when the Etaśa brought him wealth that removes reproach, bestowing it like his own allotted share.
He delivered Śuṣṇa, the insatiable devourer of Kuyava, to the charioteer Kutsa as his prey; Indra shattered the ninety-nine fortresses of Śambara for Divodāsa.
Thus have we sent forth this hymn to you, O Indra, seeking glory as if by our own strength and desiring booty.
May we, longing for it, attain that seventh [step] of the steed; may the weapon of the godless oppressor never reach us.
Thus have the Gṛtsamadas fashioned these prayers for you, O Hero, like those seeking help fashion the paths of wisdom.
Desiring sacred formulations, O Indra, may they attain through their newest hymns food, strength, a secure dwelling, and your favor.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial gift of yours yield a boon to the singer;
grant it to those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Indra, we are your strength; take note of us well. Like one seeking booty, we bring forth our hymn to you.
Singing praises and reflecting with inspired thought, we strive to win the favor of a hero such as you.
O Indra, with your protections, you guard the people who are devoted to you;
you are the lord and the protector of the one who offers oblations, for he approaches you with such focused intent.
May that Indra, our youthfully invoked friend, be auspicious as a protector for us men—
he who, with his aid, shall lead forward the one who recites, the one who exerts himself, the one who cooks, and the one who praises.
I praise that Indra, I sing his praises—he in whom men of old increased and found their strength.
May he, when implored, fulfill the desire for wealth of the devoted worshipper, the newest man of the Āyu race.
Delighting in the hymns of the Aṅgirases, Indra, the priest, struck out a path for himself;
stealing away the Dawns with the Sun while being praised, he shattered even the ancient fortresses of Aśna.
Truly renowned as Indra by name, that god has arisen for man as the most wondrous;
subduing the foe, the self-dependent one brought down the dear head of the Dāsa who acted like a leech.

That Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and destroyer of forts, drove away the Dāsa women who had black wombs. He generated for mankind both the earth and the waters; he has ever fulfilled the praise of the sacrificer.
To him, the powerful Indra, the gods have ever yielded their strength in the struggle for the waters;
when they placed the thunderbolt in his two arms, he struck down the Dasyus and shattered their iron fortresses.
Surely, O Indra, may that wealthy sacrificial fee of yours yield a boon to the singer;
grant gifts to those who praise you, let not our fortune perish. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
To him who conquers all, who conquers wealth, who conquers heaven, who conquers by sacrifice, who conquers men, who conquers fields;
to him who wins horses, who wins cattle, who wins waters—to Indra, the worshipful one, offer the beloved Soma.

To the overcomer, the shatterer, the conqueror, the invincible, the subduer, the ordainer; to the one of mighty stride, the bearer, the one whose path is hard to traverse, the ever-conquering—proclaim homage to Indra!

Ever-conquering, devourer of men, subduer of people, shaker, warrior, grown according to his pleasure; gatherer of hosts, victorious, honored among the tribes—I shall proclaim the heroic deeds performed by Indra.
The unyielding bull, the slayer of the turbulent, profound and lofty, whose wisdom is unattainable;
the impeller of the weak, the piercer, the firm, the broad—Indra, the performer of perfect sacrifice, generated the dawns and the sun.

Through sacrifice, the seekers of the path, the yearning ones who possess wisdom, have found a way across the waters; sending forth their prayers and seeking aid, they have obtained cattle through their invocations and have attained riches by impelling them toward Indra.
O Indra, bestow upon us the most excellent riches:
the insight of skill, good fortune, the increase of wealth, the safety of our bodies, the sweetness of speech, and the auspiciousness of our days.

At the Trikadruka rites, the mighty and impetuous buffalo drank his fill of the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire. It exhilarated him for the sake of performing great deeds; it accompanied him—the great and wide one. Thus the true drop attended the god Indra, the true god.
Then, radiant with brilliance, he overcame Krivi by his might in battle; he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth, with his majesty and grew even stronger.
He placed one [portion] within his belly, while the other overflowed; thus the god accompanied the god, the true Indu [the drop] accompanied true Indra.
Born together with wisdom, you have grown great with power; increased together with heroic deeds, you are the subduer of enemies, O far-seeing one.
You are the giver of wealth and desirable riches to the one who praises you; thus may the divine Soma-drop attend upon the divine Indra, the true one, as the true drop attends him.

O dancer, O Indra, that manly deed of yours was the first and ancient one, worthy of proclamation in heaven—that by the power of the god you set the life-force free and released the waters. By his might, he overcame every godless one; the Lord of a Hundred Powers found strength and found nourishment.
We invoke you, the Lord of hosts, the seer among seers, possessed of the highest renown;
the supreme king of sacred prayers, O Brahmaṇaspati, hearing us with your aids, sit upon your seat.
O Bṛhaspati, even the wise gods have obtained from you, the Asura-like one, their share of the sacrifice.
Like the sun with its light makes the cows manifest, you are the great progenitor of all sacred hymns (*brahman*).
Having driven away the surrounding waters and the darknesses, you mount the radiant chariot of Cosmic Order,
O Bṛhaspati— terrible, the subduer of enemies, the slayer of demons, the breaker of the cow-pen, and the finder of light.
With thy good guidances thou leadest and protectest the person who offers to thee; may distress never reach him.
Thou art the scorcher of those who hate prayer and the subduer of their wrath; O Bṛhaspati, such is thy great majesty.
Neither distress nor misfortune from any quarter, nor enemies, nor the double-tongued have overcome him whom you, O Brahmaṇaspati, protect as a good guardian; you drive away all deceivers from him.
You are our protector, the maker of paths, the far-seeing; for your service we age with our prayers.
O Bṛhaspati, whoever lays a snare for us, may his own fierce misfortune crush him.
Or if some mortal, a hostile enemy or a lurking wolf, would harm us though we are innocent—O Bṛhaspati, turn him away from our path; make a good way for us toward this feast of the gods.

We invoke you, the protector of our bodies, the savior, the advocate who is well-disposed toward us. O Bṛhaspati, strike down those who revile the gods; let not the evil-doers attain the highest bliss.
Through you, O Brahmanaspati, who increase us well, may we bestow upon men desirable riches.
Those enemies who are far away, those who are near, and those who assail us—crush them all, so that they have no wealth.

Through you, O Bṛhaspati, may we win the highest vital strength, through you as our fulfilling and winning ally. May the evil-minded one who seeks to harm us not prevail; may we, with our hymns of praise, cross over safely by means of our thoughts.
The bull who never yields, who goes to the battle-cry, the scorcher of the enemy, the conqueror in the hosts;
you are the true avenger of debts, O Brahmaṇaspati, the tamer even of the fierce one who exults in his strength.
He who seeks to harm us with a godless mind, thinking himself fierce and desiring to slay us—O Bṛhaspati, let his deadly weapon not reach us; we quench the wrath of that arrogant one who plots evil.
To be invoked in battles, to be approached with homage, the one who goes among the spoils and wins prize after prize—
Bṛhaspati has shattered all the attacks of the enemy who seeks to harm us, like chariots.

With your most piercing heat, O burner, burn the Rākṣasas who have held you in contempt, you whose heroism is manifest. Make manifest that power of yours which is worthy of praise; O Bṛhaspati, destroy those who surround us with their waters of malice.

O Bṛhaspati, that which belongs to the noble one, which shines forth brilliantly and powerfully among the people according to his merit— that wealth, born of the *ṛta* and radiant with might, bestow upon us as a wondrous treasure.
Do not deliver us to the thieves, those malicious enemies who lie in wait at the place of injury and greedily covet our food.
They plot against the gods in their hearts; O Bṛhaspati, they know nothing beyond this Sāman.

For Tvaṣṭṛ, the seer, brought you forth from all beings, from every *sāman*. He is the debt-collector, the debt-claimer, Brahmaṇaspati, the slayer of the deceitful, the upholder of the great cosmic order (*ṛta*).
For your glory the mountain opened wide when you, O Aṅgiras, released the herd of cattle;
with Indra as your ally, O Bṛhaspati, you unbarred the flood of waters that was encompassed by darkness.
O Brahmanaspati, be the controller of this hymn and prosper our offspring. All that which the gods favor is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Favor this offering, for you are the lord; we shall worship you with this new and great song.
O Bṛhaspati, just as our liberal patron is praised by you as a friend, so may you bring our prayer to fulfillment.

He who, by his might, made those who were not to be bowed down bow; who with fury shattered the strongholds of Śambara; who caused even the unshakable things to fall—Brahmaṇaspati entered the mountain rich in treasures and split it asunder.
That was the deed for the most divine among the gods: they loosened what was firm and made the solid things yield.
He drove forth the cows, split Vala with his sacred prayer, concealed the darkness, and made the light of heaven visible.
Brahmaṇaspati pierced with might that well whose mouth was stone, which had a stream of honey;
all those who behold the light of heaven drank from it, and together they poured forth the watery spring in abundance.
Ancient indeed are those beings that have come into existence; through months and autumns, they have opened wide the doors for you.
Moving one after another without ceasing, Brahmaṇaspati has established these various pathways.

Those who, approaching, reached that treasure of the Paṇis—the supreme one hidden in the cave—they, being wise, having perceived the falsehoods, returned; from where they had come, they rose up again to enter.
The truth-abiding sages, having discerned the falsehoods, returned once more from there and stood upon the great paths.
They [found] the fire kindled by their two arms upon the stone; for there is no one who is a stranger to it, since they have abandoned that [falsehood].
With his swift bow strung with *ṛta*, Brahmaṇaspati reaches whatever he desires;
excellent are his arrows wherewith he shoots—those who behold men and whose source is the ear, that they may see.
He is the one who leads the host, he is the one who disciplines; he is the domestic priest, he is the well-praised Lord of Prayer (*brahmaṇaspati*) in battle.
When the powerful one brings forth booty through inspired thought, then the sun shines from that wealth, burning with fervor at will.

The far-reaching and sovereign Bṛhaspati, the first of those who bestow abundance, possesses most gracious and successful gifts. These are the attainments of the desirable and powerful one, by which both classes of people—the clans—enjoy their sustenance.
He who is all-pervading in the lower enclosure, great and most delightful, has grown strong with power;
that god has spread himself wide against the gods, for he, Brahmaṇaspati, encompasses them all.
O Maghavans, all truth belongs to you alone; even the waters do not violate your ordinance.
O Indra and Brahmaṇaspati, come to our oblation and food like two prize-winning steeds yoked together.

And the swiftest bearers hear [his call]; the eloquent one, fit for the assembly, wins wealth through his inspired thoughts. With firm hatred, he who collects debts according to his will—he indeed is the prize-winning *Brahmaṇaspati* in the encounter.
The true wrath of Brahmaṇaspati became according to his will as he was about to perform great deeds;
he who drove out the cows distributed them to heaven, and like a mighty stream, he flowed forth separately by his own might.
O Brahmanaspati, may we ever be masters of well-governed wealth that provides vital strength;
bestow heroic sons upon our heroes, since you, as the sovereign lord, come to my invocation through this sacred prayer.
O Brahmanaspati, be the controller of this hymn and prosper our offspring. All that which the gods favor is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Kindling the fire, he shall conquer those who seek to harm him; having offered prayers and presented oblations, he shall prosper.
He surpasses every being born with that which was already born—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
With heroes he shall conquer heroes who attack; he shall spread his wealth with cattle and be mindful by himself.
His offspring and his descendants increase—whomever Brahmanaspati makes his ally.
Like the surging flood of the Sindhu, he is impetuous and fierce; like a bull against castrated oxen, he overcomes his enemies with might.
Like the spreading flame of Agni, he cannot be turned back—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
For him flow the celestial, inexhaustible [streams]; as the first among beings, he goes forth for the sake of cattle.
With unabated power, he slays by his might whomever Brahmanaspati makes his ally.
For him all the roaring rivers flow; they have provided many flawless protections.
Blessed in the favor of the gods, he prospers—whomever Brahmanaspati makes his ally.

The upright singer shall conquer those who attack him; the one seeking the gods shall prevail over the godless. The well-aided man shall conquer in battles that are hard to overcome; the sacrificer shall divide the food away from the non-sacrificer.
Sacrifice, O hero; go forth to those who desire you; form an auspicious mind for the conquest of Vṛtra.
Prepare the oblation so that you may be fortunate; we choose the protection of Brahmaṇaspati.
He indeed, with his people, with his clan, with his kin, and with his sons, wins booty and wealth through his men—
he who, with a mind full of faith, seeks to win over Brahmaṇaspati, the father of the gods, with an oblation.
Whosoever has honored him with oblations rich in ghee—him Brahmaṇaspati leads forward.
He delivers him from distress, protects him from harm; even from great danger, the wondrous one makes wide room for him.
These songs, dripping with clarity, I ever offer with the ladle to the Ādityas, the kings.
May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, the many-born Varuṇa, Dakṣa, and Aṃśa hear us.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, acting with one accord, accept this hymn of mine today—
the Ādityas, who are pure, cleansed by the stream, free from crookedness, blameless, and unharmed.
Those Ādityas—vast, profound, undeceived, many-eyed, and seeking to harm—behold both the crooked and the straight within; for these kings, even the most distant things are near at hand.
The Ādityas support that which moves and that which stands; they are gods, the guardians of the entire world.
Far-sighted, they protect their divine power, upholding the cosmic order and exacting the payment of debts.
O Ādityas, may I obtain this knowledge of your aid, O Aryaman, which brings comfort even in the midst of fear.
Under your guidance, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I avoid all difficulties as one avoids a pit.
For easy to travel is your path, O Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa—thornless and straight. By that path, O Ādityas, speak for us and grant us a protection that is difficult to overcome.
May Aditi, the mother of kings, and Aryaman carry us across all hostilities by easy paths.
May we, possessing many heroes and unharmed, abide under the great protection of Mitra and Varuṇa.
Supporting the three earths and the three heavens, they maintain the three laws within their assembly.
By the Eternal Order, O Ādityas, your greatness is mighty; that majesty of yours, O Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra, is beautiful.
They uphold the three celestial luminaries; golden-hued, pure, and purified by their own radiance;
sleepless, unblinking, undeceived, and far-famed, they exist for the sake of the upright mortal.
O Varuṇa, you are the king of all—both those who are gods, O Asura, and those who are mortals. Grant us a hundred autumns to behold; may we attain the well-established lifespans of former times.
Neither the right nor the left is distinguished, neither the east, O Ādityas, nor the west.
Whether we are simple or wise, O Vasus, may we, led by you, attain the light that is free from fear.
He who offers gifts to the kings who uphold the cosmic order (*ṛta*), and whom constant prosperities cause to grow—
he, wealthy, goes first in his chariot, a giver of goods, praised in the sacrificial assemblies.
Pure, with good pastures, undeceived, and possessing brave sons, he dwells among the waters, having reached old age.
No one slays him, neither from near nor from afar, who abides under the guidance of the Ādityas.
O Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, be gracious, whatever offense we may have committed against you.
May I attain the wide, fearless light; O Indra, let not the long darknesses overtake us.

Both worlds, turning toward him, cause the rain from heaven to swell for him; nourishing his auspicious name, he goes forth conquering both dwellings. Both halves of the world become favorable to him.

O worshipful Ādityas, those illusions of yours for the treacherous, and those snares spread out for the enemy—may we pass over them like a charioteer with his chariot; may we remain unharmed within your wide protection.

O Varuṇa, may I not experience the destitution of a dear, liberal, and bountiful friend. O King, may we not be deprived of well-governed wealth. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak loudly at the assembly.
May all these things of the poet Āditya, the self-ruling king, prevail by his greatness.
He who is the delightful god for sacrifice—I beg for the high renown of the abundant Varuṇa.
Under your law, O Varuṇa, may we be fortunate, praising you with devoted minds;
as days pass, may we approach the dawns rich in cattle, like fires that burn through the days.
May we be in the protection of you, O Varuṇa, leader of wide renown, who possess many heroes.
O undeceived sons of Aditi, O gods, grant us your favor for our alliance.
The Āditya, the Ordainer, has sent them forth; the rivers flow according to the Law (*ṛta*) of Varuṇa.
They do not weary, nor do they cease; like birds they fly swiftly across the expanse of the earth.

Loosen for me my sin like a rope; may we succeed in finding the spring of your *ṛta*, O Varuṇa. Let not the thread be severed while I weave my prayer; let not my measure be shattered before the time of the work.
O Varuṇa, drive the fear away from me; O sovereign Lord of Truth, hold me in accordance with the *ṛta*.
Release me from distress as one releases a calf from its tether; for not even for a moment can anyone exist far from you.

O Varuṇa, do not strike us with those weapons of yours, O Asura, which consume the one who commits sin while performing your rites. May we not go forth from the light; utterly loosen our adversaries so that we may live.
Homage to you, O Varuṇa, both now and in the past, and even hereafter, O many-born one, we shall speak. For in you alone, O invincible one, are established those unshakable laws, like mountains.

Deliver me from the debts contracted by me; O King, let me not suffer for what others have done. There are yet many dawns that have not dawned; O Varuṇa, while we are still alive, establish us within them.
O King, whether it be one who is my ally or my friend, who has spoken of fear to me in my dream while I am afraid; or whoever, like a thief or a wolf, seeks to harm us—O Varuṇa, protect us from that!
O Varuṇa, may I not experience the destitution of a dear, bountiful, and liberal patron;
O King, may we not be deprived of well-governed wealth. May we, blessed with heroic sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Ādityas, upholders of sacred vows, vigorous ones, keep my sin far away like a woman who has borne in secret.
O gods Varuṇa and Mitra, you who hear me and know what is auspicious—I call upon you for protection.
O gods, you are our providence; you are our strength. Drive away our enemies to a distance.
As those who bestow gifts, look upon us with favor and be patient; show us mercy this day and in the days to come.
O Vasus, what indeed may we do for you with future friendship, or what with past alliance?
O Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Indra, and Maruts, grant us well-being.
O gods, you indeed are our kinsmen; have mercy upon me who implores you.
Let not your chariot be held back midway by the wind, nor let us grow weary among those who are not your kin.
One [of you], O gods, has forgiven my many offenses when you instructed me like a father instructs a gambler.
Keep your snares far away, keep misfortunes far away; do not seize me, O gods, as one seizes a bird in its young.
O worshipful ones, turn toward us this day; fearing, I would enter into your heart.
O gods, protect us from the devouring wolf; protect us, O worshipful ones, from the pit and from falling.

O Varuṇa, may I not suffer loss from my dear patron, the generous giver; may I not fall away from the well-governed wealth of my friend, O King. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The waters do not rest for Savitṛ, the god who ordains the cosmic order (ṛta), nor for Indra, the slayer of Ahi.
Day after day the darkness of the waters passes away; how great is the first emission of them?
The Mother spoke forth to the wise one who was about to bring a snare for Vṛtra:
"Cutting out paths according to his pleasure, the roaring rivers go day after day toward their goal."
For he stood upright in the mid-air and then hurled his weapon at Vṛtra;
clothed in mist, Indra rushed upon him and, armed with sharp weapons, conquered the enemy.
O Bṛhaspati, pierce the heroes of the Asura Vṛkadvaras with your heat, like a blazing fire!
Just as you have boldly struck them down even in the past, so now, O Indra, slay our enemy.
Cast down from on high the stone from heaven, with which, being exhilarated, you may utterly consume the enemy.
For the winning of offspring, of many descendants, and of cattle, O Indra, make us your equal share.
For you two increase the mental power which you both desire; you are the inciters of the worshipper who exerts himself.
O Indra and Soma, protect us both; in this time of fear, create for us a place of safety.

Let neither exhaustion, nor fatigue, nor sloth overcome me; let us not say, "Do not press the Soma," to him who gives to me, who bestows upon me, who takes heed of me, and who approaches me with cattle when I am pressing the juice.
O Sarasvatī, protect us; accompanied by the Maruts, you boldly conquer our enemies.
Even that arrogant one, exulting in his strength—the bull of the Śaṇḍikas—Indra slays him.
Whoever seeks to harm us from afar or whoever would strike us down—beholding him, pierce him with your sharpened weapon!
O Bṛhaspati, conquer the enemies with your arms; O King, deliver the one who seeks to injure us into the power of the malicious.
O Hero, with our own heroic warriors, perform those deeds of valor which are yours to do. Let them long remain smoldering; having slain them, bring back their riches to us.
Seeking your favor, I address with reverence and homage this divine host, the Marut troop,
so that we may obtain wealth consisting of all-heroic sons, accompanied by progeny, and renowned day by day.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect our chariot together with the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus,
as we fly forth like birds from our dwelling, seeking glory, exultant, and seated upon the trees.
And so, O gods, being of one accord, protect our chariot that seeks booty among the people;
when the swift steeds, crossing the dust with their feet, strike it down with their hooves upon the ridge of the earth.
And may that Indra, the lord of all people, the one of excellent wisdom, come with the host of Maruts from heaven;
may he follow our chariot with his safe protections for the sake of great gain and the winning of booty.
And may that god Tvaṣṭṛ, the overcomer of the world, in harmony with the divine wives, speed forth the chariot;
may Iḷā, Bhaga, Bṛhaddivā, the two worlds, Pūṣan, Purandhi, and the Aśvins, the lords, likewise do so.
And those two auspicious goddesses, Dawn and Night, who look upon each other and incite the movement of all living beings—
I praise you both, O Earth, with a new hymn, as I spread out for the stationary world a threefold layer of vital strength.
And may Ahi Budhnya,
Aja Ekapād, Trita, R̥bhukṣan, Savitṛ, and Apāṃ Napāt— the swift impeller— grant us favor through our prayer and our ritual labor, as they do for the Uśijs.
These [songs] I desire for you, O worshipful ones, which the Āyus have fashioned together as something new.
Seeking glory and longing for booty, may they reach our prayer like a chariot-horse.

O Heaven and Earth, be the protectors of this my word, which seeks to win the truth; you whose life-span is further than this, I, seeking wealth, place you—the two highly praised ones—before me in greatness.
Let not secret injuries from mortal man harm us on this day; do not deliver us over to these calamities.
Let our friendship not be severed; take note of that with a mind seeking our welfare—for that very thing we entreat you.
With a mind free from malice, bring hither swift obedience; you who are the milch-cow, overflowing, swelling with milk, and inexhaustible.
O you invoked by many, I urge you evermore—swift with your feet and powerful with your word.
I invoke Rākā, who is easily summoned, with a beautiful hymn; may the fortunate one hear us and take notice of us herself.
May she sew together our work with a needle that does not break, and may she grant us a praiseworthy hero-son who bestows hundreds of gifts.
O Rākā, those benevolent thoughts of yours which are well-formed, by which you bestow riches upon the donor—
with those, come to us today with a gracious mind, O fortunate one, granting us thousandfold prosperity.
O Sinīvālī, broad-tressed one, you who are the sister of the gods—enjoy the offered oblation; O goddess, grant us progeny.
To her who has beautiful arms, lovely fingers, who is well-nourished and prolific of offspring—
to that Sinīvālī, the mistress of the people, offer the oblation.
Gungū, Sinīvālī, Rākā, and Sarasvatī—
Indrāṇī I have invoked for aid, and Varuṇānī for well-being.
O Father of the Maruts, let your favor come to us; do not deprive us of the sight of the sun.
May your hero be gracious toward our horse; may we, O Rudra, be propagated with offspring.
O Rudra, through these most auspicious medicines bestowed by you, may I attain a hundred winters. Drive far away from us hatred, drive away distress, and drive away diseases in all directions.
O Rudra, you are the most excellent of all that is born by virtue of your splendor; you are the strongest among the strong, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
Carry us across to the further shore of distress with well-being; ward off all assaults of the malicious.
O Rudra, let us not provoke you to anger with our prostrations, nor with ill-praises, O Bull, nor with joint invocations.
Raise up our heroes with your medicines; I hear that you are the best of physicians among physicians.
With invocations and oblations, I would turn Rudra toward me with my hymns—he who is invoked by those seeking his call.
May he of the soft belly, the one easy to invoke, the tawny one with beautiful jaws, not deliver us over to this thoughtlessness.
The bull, accompanied by the Maruts, has gladdened me with his most vigorous strength as I implored him.
Like one seeking shade from the heat, may I, free from harm, attain the favor of Rudra; may I win his goodwill.
O Rudra, where is that merciful hand of yours which possesses healing medicine and cooling relief? O Bull, as the remover of divine affliction, look now with favor upon me.
To the brown, white-shining bull, I send forth a great and mighty hymn of praise. With prostrations we honor the radiant one; we celebrate the fierce name of Rudra with our salutations.
With firm limbs, multiform, fierce, and tawny, he has adorned himself with bright gold ornaments.
From Rudra, the lord of this vast world, let not his divine power ever depart.
Worthy, you carry arrows and a bow; worthy, you wear the worshipful, multiform golden breastplate.
Worthy, you bestow all this vast power upon us; O Rudra, there is nothing more mighty than you.
Praise the famous one, who sits upon the chariot-seat, the youthful, fierce, and striking hunter like a dread beast.
O Rudra, being praised, be gracious to the singer; let your missiles strike down someone other than us.
Even a youth bows before his father who approaches him with reverence; O Rudra, you praise the lord of the virtuous, the giver of abundant wealth. Being praised, may you grant us medicines.
O Maruts, those pure medicines of yours, which are most healing, O heroes, and which bring delight;
those which Manu chose for us, our father—I desire those auspicious and beneficial ones of Rudra.
May the missile of Rudra avoid us; may the great ill-will of the impetuous one pass us by.
O Bounteous One, relax your firm [bow] for our patrons; have mercy on our children and descendants.

Thus, O tawny bull, manifesting yourself, O God, so that you neither grow angry nor strike us down—be here today, O Rudra, hearing our invocation. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The Maruts, who pour down rain, bold in their might, terrifying like wild beasts with their powers and resplendent in their brilliance;
glowing like fires, impetuous in their course, they blew away the whirlwind and disclosed the cattle.
Like the heavens with their stars, the ring-adorned ones have shone forth; like rain from a cloud, they have flashed out.
O Maruts, with Rudra as your leader, you who wear golden ornaments upon your chests, he was born from the bright udder of Pṛśni.
They groom their horses like coursers in the races, hastening with the swift ears of the river.
O Maruts, wearing golden helmets and shaking [your spears], you who are of one mind, come with your spotted deer to our nourishment.
They have grown strong to nourish all these worlds, or rather, they are ever-givers of life for Mitra;
with spotted deer as their steeds, possessing inexhaustible wealth, they stand at the yoke like swift-flying birds upon their paths.

With your blazing spears, come like swans to their own resting places, O Maruts of one mind, along dustless paths with your swelling-milking, roaring-cow steeds that are free from stain, for the exhilaration of the sweet draught.
O Maruts, of one mind, come to our prayers and to our libations like the praise of men;
swell us like a mare, like a cow with her udder; and make the prayer for the singer adorned with strength.
O Maruts, grant us that vigorous chariot, a prayer that awakens our understanding day by day;
grant nourishment to the singers, and to the poet in the assemblies, a prize of wisdom, inviolable and invincible strength.
When the Maruts, with golden ornaments upon their chests, yoke their horses to the chariots, O Bounteous Bhaga;
then, like a cow swelling for her calf in the stalls, you pour forth great nourishment for the people who offer oblations.
O Maruts, O Vasus, if a mortal enemy should set himself against us with wolfish intent, protect us from harm!
Turn him back with your glowing wheel; O Rudras, strike down the weapon of the one who curses us.
O Maruts, that wondrous journey of yours is renowned, when the kinsmen milked even the udder of Pṛśni;
or when you, O sons of Rudra, infallible ones, brought Trita to old age for the sake of reproach against the one who reviles.
We invoke you, the great Maruts, who move swiftly like birds, at the offering of the rushing Viṣṇu;
with uplifted ladles and devoted to sacred prayer, we, the seekers of divine power, implore you for glorious wealth.
Those Daśagvas first brought the sacrifice; may they urge us on at the dawning of the mornings.
Like Dawn, she uncovers the dark nights with her ruddy beams, with great, glowing light that swells with a flood of kine.
Those Rudras have grown strong in the seats of Cosmic Order, together with the celestial waters and their ruddy ointments;
raining down with impetuous vigor, they have assumed a most radiant and well-fashioned hue.
Approaching for great protection and aid, we indeed praise them with this homage— those whom Trita, as if for his own assistance, brought hither from afar to help, like the five Hotṛ-priests.

That aid by which you carry the distressed across distress, and by which you release the worshipper from reproach—O Maruts, let that favor of yours come hither; let your benevolence speed toward us like a lowing cow.
Seeking booty, I have sent forth this eloquent prayer; may the Eater accept my songs with favor.
Will not the Son of the Waters, who impels swift horses, make them well-adorned? For he indeed shall take pleasure in them.
Let us speak this mantra, well-fashioned from our hearts, to him; will he indeed take note of it?
The Son of the Waters, by the greatness of his divine power, has brought forth all the worlds of the noble one.
Some flow together, others approach; the rivers fill the common ocean.
Around him, the pure waters have gathered—the bright, shining Son of the Waters.
The waters, like smiling maidens, go around that youth, cleansing him;
he, bright with his radiant powers, shines richly for us—unfanned by wood, clothed in ghee, within the waters.
For him, the three unshakable goddesses, the divine women, present food for the god.
For he has glided forth into the waters like prepared [offerings]; he drinks the first-milk of those who have borne before.
Herein is the birthplace of the horse and of this [sun]; protect the patrons from the malicious, from harm, and from those who would assail us.
Beyond the raw fortresses, he is unassailable; there the enemies shall perish, as shall all falsehoods.
He in whose own home is a cow that yields milk well—he swells with his own vital power and eats excellent food.
That Son of the Waters, bestowing strength within the waters, shines forth for the sake of granting wealth to the one who serves him.
He who, true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), eternal, and pure by divine nature, shines far and wide within the waters;
from him all other beings are born like branches, and the plants are produced through his progeny.
For the Son of the Waters has indeed taken his seat in the lap of the prostrate ones, standing upright and clothed in lightning.
Carrying his supreme majesty, the youthful, gold-colored rivers flow around him.
Golden in form, golden in appearance, the Son of the Waters is indeed golden-hued;
having sat down from his golden womb, the givers of gold offer food to him.
That countenance of his, and his lovely name, the secret one, increases—the grandson of the waters—whom the young maidens thus kindle together; he is golden-hued, and clarified butter is his food.
To him, the nearest friend among many, let us do service with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations.
I polish his back, I provide for him with hollowed logs, I nourish him with food, and I celebrate him all around with hymns.
He, the bull, begat the embryo in them; as an infant he sucks them, and they lick him.
He, the Son of Waters, of unblemished hue, has here entered another’s body as it were with his own form.
Upon this highest step, standing firm, shining forever with stainless rays—
unto him, his own offspring, the youthful waters fly around, bringing ghee as food in their garments.

O Agni, I have offered a secure dwelling for the people, and I have offered a well-fashioned hymn to the patrons. All that which the gods favor is auspicious. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
For you, the waters and the cows have been sent forth; the men have milked them out with the woolly stones.
O Indra, drink the Soma offered with *svāhā* and consecrated with *vaṣaṭ* from the Hotṛ’s cup—you who are the first lord of it.
Mingled with sacrifices, with spotted deer and spears, you radiant ones, dear in your ornaments, come on your journey;
having sat upon the sacrificial grass of Bharata, O sons of Heaven, O heroes, drink the Soma from the Potar’s cup.
Come indeed to us, you who are easy to invoke; sit down upon the sacrificial grass and take your delight.
Then, O Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-pleased with the soma juice, rejoice together with the gods and their wives in your excellent company.

O sage, bring the gods here and sacrifice; O Hotṛ, sit down upon the three seats. Accept the Soma-sweetness that has been set forth; drink from the Āgnīdhra-vessel and satisfy yourself with your portion.
This [Soma] is indeed the increaser of your manly strength for your body; from of old, power has been placed within your arms.
Pressed for you, O Maghavan, it is brought for you; drink of it to your heart's content from this priestly bowl.

May you both enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. The Hotṛ priest has sat down according to the ancient invocations. O Kings, homage comes toward you; drink the Soma-sweetness from the Praśāstṛ.

Rejoice according to your pleasure from the oblation of the Soma juice, O Adhvaryus; he desires the full ladle poured out. Bring this to him, for he is the giver who seeks it; O Draviṇodas, drink the Soma from the oblation with the seasonal rites.
Him whom I invoked before, him I invoke now; he indeed is to be invoked, he who rules over the name "Giver.
O Giver of Wealth, drink with the seasons the Soma-sweetness set forth by the Adhvaryus from the Potar’s cup.

May the sacrificial fires by which you travel be fat for you; O Lord of the Forest, be firm and do not fail. Drawing near and summoning [the gods], O bold one, drink the Soma from the Neṣṭṛ’s vessel with the seasons, O Giver of Wealth.

From the office of the Hotṛ he has drunk, and from the Potṛ he has been exhilarated; from the Neṣṭṛ he has enjoyed the prepared food. May Draviṇodas drink from the fourth cup—the uninjured, immortal one—of him who bestows wealth.
Yoke today your chariot that comes hitherward, which is swift and drawn by men; let its unyoking be here for you both.
Mix the oblations with honey, for it has arrived; then drink the Soma, O you who possess abundant wealth.
O Agni, accept the fuel; accept the oblation; accept the prayer of the people; accept the beautiful hymn of praise.
O Vasu, with all [the gods] and according to the season, being great, desiring [them], make the yearning gods drink the oblation.
Up has risen this god Savitṛ for his impulsion; the bearer of the oblation has stood firm for that most constant act.
Now indeed he bestows treasure upon the gods; thus he has granted a share in well-being to the one who offers the sacrifice with welcome.
For, standing erect with broad hands, the God extends his arms so that all may hear;
even the waters bend down at his command, and even this wind rests while moving around the earth.
Even those who travel on swift steeds he now unyokes; he has brought even the weary traveler to rest from his journey.
He has restrained even the rushing waters; desiring to help, he has come according to the ordinance of Savitṛ.
Weaving it out, she has stretched it across again; the wise one has placed his skill within the reach of the maker.
Having gathered it up, he has stood forth; he has distributed the seasons. Savitar, the god, has come with his readiness.
The doors spread wide like many ships; the flame of Agni extends through the whole span of life.
The Mother has bestowed the most excellent portion upon her son, according to his desire impelled by Savitṛ.
He who was stationed there, desiring to conquer, has returned; the desire of all those wandering abroad has come home.
Having cast off his changed form, he has come according to the ordinance of the divine Savitṛ.
The waters have spread out their watery portion set by you within the waters; the thirsty ones have wandered through the desert lands.
No one violates these ordinances of the god Savitṛ, which he has established for the birds and the forests.

As Varuṇa, swiftly moving, reaches the watery womb that is not to be pierced even in a moment, so every bird has entered its nest; Savitṛ has distributed all living beings according to their stations.
He whose sacred law neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman, nor Rudra violates—
nor do the enemies— I invoke that god Savitar here for well-being with prostrations.
Seeking fortune, insight, and abundance, may Narāśaṃsa and the Lord of the Goddesses protect us;
may we be dear to the god Savitṛ at the gathering of wealth and the attainment of all that is desirable.
May that desirable wealth, granted by you from heaven, from the waters, and from the earth, come to us—
wealth that shall be a blessing for our praisers, for our kinsman, and for the singer who extols you widely, O Savitṛ.

Like two pressing-stones, you two indeed exert yourselves for this purpose; like two vultures toward a tree containing a treasure, like two priests at the assembly chanting hymns, like two messengers with offerings for many people.
Setting out at dawn like two chariot-warriors, like two heroes, you two, the twins, pursue our choice;
adorning your bodies like two women, you are like a husband and wife who find wisdom among the people.
Come toward us like two horns, moving swiftly like two hooves with your aids;
