come hither at the break of dawn like a pair of ruddy geese, O mighty ones, like two chariot wheels.
Like two boats, carry us across; like two yokes, like two nave-pieces, like two inner wheels, and like two outer wheels;
like two dogs that do not fail our bodies, and like two crutches, protect us from falling apart.
Like the wind, you are undecaying; like the flow of rivers, come hither with your eye as with two eyes.
Like hands most beneficial to the body, like feet, lead us toward greater prosperity.
Like two lips speaking honey from the mouth, like two breasts, nourish us so that we may live. Like two nostrils, be the protectors of our bodies; like two ears, be well-hearing for us.
Like two hands, bestow power upon us; like two feet, traverse for us the realms of space. O Aśvins, sharpen these songs of ours directed toward you, as one sharpens an axe with a whetstone.
O Aśvins, these strengthening prayers, this hymn of praise, the Gṛtsamadas have fashioned for you.
O Heroes, graciously accept them; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Soma and Pūṣan, begetters of riches, begetters of heaven, begetters of earth,
born as the guardians of the entire world, the gods have made you the navel of immortality.
May these two gods, at their birth, be pleased; may they conceal the hated darkness.
For these two, Soma and Pūṣan, Indra produced the cooked [milk] within the raw cows.
O Soma and Pūṣan, you two, O Bulls, quicken that seven-wheeled chariot which measures the mid-region, which never fails, which turns in all directions, is yoked by thought, and has five reins.
One has made his dwelling high in heaven; the other is upon the earth and in the mid-air.
May those two disclose for us an abundance of many desirable things and much food—the increase of wealth and our very kinship.
One has generated all beings; the other moves along beholding the universe.
O Soma and Pūṣan, favor my prayer; with you two may we conquer all hostile armies.
May Pūṣan, the inspirer of all, quicken our prayer; may Soma, the lord of wealth, bestow riches upon us.
May the goddess Aditi, who is free from enemies, protect us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Vāyu, with those thousand chariots of yours, come hither, drawn by your teams of horses,
to drink the Soma.
O Vāyu, come with your team of horses; this bright [soma] is offered to you.
You shall go to the house of the one who presses the juice.
O Indra and Vāyu, masters of the teams of horses, come today to the bright soma mixed with milk;
drink it, O heroes.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of Truth, this Soma has been pressed for you;
hear my invocation here.
The two kings, free from malice, sit upon the firm and highest seat,
on a throne with a thousand pillars.
Those two sovereign kings, the Ādityas, who drink the clarified butter and are lords of bounty,
dwell together in a place free from reproach.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come hither with cattle and with horses;
O Rudras, lords of men, come to our dwelling.
O you who possess abundant wealth, let no enemy from afar nor any from near,
no malevolent mortal foe, prevail against us.
O Aśvins, you who are worthy of praise and finders of wide space, bring hither to us wealth of golden hue.
Indra indeed shall drive away even great fear;
for he is steadfast and active among all people.
May Indra be gracious to us; may no evil reach us from behind;
may there be prosperity for us from the front.
May Indra grant us freedom from fear from all directions; he is the conqueror of enemies, the one who observes all people.
O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation.
Sit down upon this sacrificial grass.
This intense, honey-sweet, exhilarating draught is for you among the Śunahotras;
drink this desirable one.
With Indra as their chief, the hosts of Maruts, the gods whose gifts are from Pūṣan—
may all of them hear my call.
O Sarasvatī, most expansive, best of rivers, most divine!
We are, as it were, unworthy of praise; O Mother, grant us renown.
In you, O goddess Sarasvatī, all lifespans are centered;
rejoice among the Śunahotras, O goddess, and grant us progeny.
O Sarasvatī, rich in sacrificial food, accept these prayers;
O observer of Truth, those beloved thoughts which the Gṛtsamadas offer to you among the gods.
We choose you two here, Agni and the bearer of oblations, who are auspicious and bring prosperity to the sacrifice.
May Heaven and Earth today present this successful, heaven-reaching sacrifice of ours among the gods.
May the gods worthy of sacrifice, free from malice, sit upon your lap here today for the drinking of Soma.
Crying out repeatedly, proclaiming his birth, he sends forth his voice like a rower propelling a boat.
O auspicious bird, may you be a bringer of good fortune; let no misfortune from any quarter find you.
May the hawk not strike you down, nor the eagle; may the arrow-bearing hero who shoots not find you.
Crying out toward the direction of your ancestors, you, auspicious and speaking blessings, speak here.

Cry out from the right side of our houses, O bird, you who are auspicious and a speaker of blessings! Let not the thief nor the malevolent man have power over us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
The singers praise him from the right, like birds, the winged ones speaking in due season;
like a Sāman-singer, he utters both voices, and he shines forth according to the Gāyatrī and the Triṣṭubh meters.
Like a *udgātṛ* priest, O bird, you sing the *sāman*; like a son of a Brahmin, you recite at the soma-pressings.
Like a stallion, you go toward the mother-cows; O bird, proclaim auspiciousness for us from every side, O bird, proclaim merit for us from all sides!
O bird, as you speak, utter auspicious words; sitting silently, be mindful of our well-being.
When you fly up, let your cry be like that of the *karkari* lute. May we, blessed with heroic sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
